Internship Opportunity: GTM Software Development at Outlio
We're offering a 3 month internship in software development with Outlio, a leading Pakistani GTM tech company.
However it's unpaid
What you'll learn and work on
• Hands-on software development
• Data engineering
• System development and architecture
• Current, in-demand industry tools, technologies, and practices
• Real operations on Outlier's own software and several other platforms
What you'll receive
• A certified internship certificate, provided to every intern
• An appreciation letter for strong performance
• The possibility of a paid, full-time role for top performers

About The Company
At Naval Nuclear Laboratory (NNL), our work supports the safety and reliability of the nation’s naval nuclear reactors and helps train the Sailors who operate them aboard U.S. Navy submarines and aircraft carriers. For more than 75 years, we have developed advanced nuclear propulsion technology, provided technical support, and trained world-class nuclear operators. NNL is a national asset dedicated solely to the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program, relying on the contributions of nearly 8,000 engineers, scientists, technicians, and support professionals.
NNL is operated for the U.S. Department of Energy by Fluor Marine Propulsion, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Fluor Corporation. Our teams work at DOE facilities and other locations supporting the program. We foster a culture grounded in trust, empowerment, and collaboration, with a shared commitment to meaningful work and high standards of safety and reliability.
About The Role
Naval Nuclear Laboratory’s Information Technology Department is seeking an Entry-Level Software Developer to support custom and low-code application development. In this role, you will contribute to the design, development, testing, and maintenance of business applications that help meet user and organizational needs. You will work with both low-code platforms and traditional programming languages, collaborating with experienced developers and stakeholders in a structured, team-oriented environment.
This opportunity is suited to a curious and motivated early-career professional who enjoys solving problems and is ready to learn new technologies. You will help create workflows, forms, dashboards, integrations, and custom application features while developing your technical skills and learning established development, security, and quality practices.
Qualifications
Applicants must have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in a related field from an accredited college or university. Familiarity with software development fundamentals—including variables, data structures, debugging, testing, and version control—is preferred. Exposure to low-code or no-code platforms such as Microsoft Power Platform or ServiceNow is helpful, though a willingness to learn these tools is also valued.
Preferred qualifications include a basic understanding of web technologies such as HTML, CSS, REST APIs, JSON, and client-server architecture, as well as awareness of secure coding, access controls, data handling, and software quality principles. Successful candidates bring analytical and troubleshooting skills, communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical colleagues, and are eager to learn platforms, standards, and business processes. All candidates must be U.S. citizens. Selected applicants will undergo a federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified matter.
Responsibilities
Assist with developing, testing, and maintaining business applications using low-code platforms and traditional programming languages. Build and update workflows, forms, dashboards, integrations, and application features in response to user and business requirements. Work with senior developers and stakeholders to understand needs, clarify requirements, and contribute to practical software solutions.
Help troubleshoot application issues, investigate defects, and support testing to verify that solutions function as intended. Document development work, technical decisions, and troubleshooting steps so that solutions can be understood and maintained by the team. Follow established coding practices, security requirements, access controls, and quality standards. Continue building technical knowledge and contribute constructively to a collaborative development environment.
Benefits
NNL offers a comprehensive benefits package that may include health, dental, and vision coverage; voluntary benefits; disability, life, and accident insurance; a 401(k) savings program; and a Capital Accumulation Plan. Additional offerings include personal and medical time off, paid parental leave, flexible work schedules, tuition assistance for eligible employees, a student debt benefit, a personal time-off sell program, an Employee Assistance Program, and wellness resources.
The annual pay range for this position is $63,900 to $97,800. Salary is a general guideline and is determined based on experience, qualifications, market factors, and business considerations. FMP maintains a drug-free workplace. Candidates must pass a drug test in accordance with company policy and applicable federal requirements; testing includes marijuana, which remains illegal under federal law.
Equal Opportunity
Fluor Marine Propulsion, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veterans. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, sex, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law.

experience:

, including

My planning recommendation:
Be ready to respond when clarifications arrive, and allow approximately
two weeks after the apparent-awardee announcement for award and eLibrary listing
. That’s a planning reference based on this client’s experience, not a guaranteed timeline.

Keep watching
OASIS+ Award Announcements
under GSA’s continuously open solicitations page, then check
GSA eLibrary
for your listing.

The United States Senate Veterans Affairs Committee (SVAC) advanced out of committee several nominees:

 👉 Maria Chapa Lopez, who served in the US Army and as US attorney for U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida, to be chair of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Board of Veterans Appeals

 👉 VA Deputy General Counsel Robert R. Fleck, US Army judge advocate David M. Jones, US Army judge advocate Daniel Rendleman and former congressional staffer James L. Quinn to sit on the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC), which reviews appeals of Board decisions

 👉 Gary W. Shatswell, a senior advisor to VA Secretary Doug Collins and former chief information officer at Unilever Prestige, to be the VA's assistant secretary for information and technology

The Senate will next consider whether they should be appointed.

There are several big items on the lawyers' agenda, so they may be hitting the ground running:

 1️⃣ Taming the appeals docket at the Board and CAVC, with Vietnam-era veterans aging out of the workforce and increasingly turning to the VA for disability compensation and access the healthcare, only to be denied benefits

 2️⃣ Responding to legislation proposed by Senators Jim Bank and Bill Cassidy and Representatives Mike Bost and Morgan Luttrell that, if enacted, would study the possibility of the Board issuing precedential opinions

 3️⃣ Exploring the role of the CAVC in deciding constitutional questions, in the event that The Supreme Court of the United States decides that the CAVC is the appropriate forum to entertain constitutional challenges to veterans benefits laws

As for Shatswell, he'll be looking to roll out the VA's ambitious electronic health records modernization (#EHRM), as it faces scrutiny over increased costs and questions about cybersecurity.

SVAC recently took testimony related to #EHRM this week, and the U.S. House of Representatives Veterans Affairs Committee (HVAC) will be hearing from Oracle's CEO Michael Sicilia and Executive Vice President Seema Verma on November 19, 2026.
